newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on Yeltsin recovery.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on Yeltsin recovery.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Wednesday on local demand, and traders anticipated a rise next week as Western investors digest the news that President Boris Yeltsin is recovering well from heart surgery.
Traders forecast a rise after the November 7-9 holidays in Russia, when markets are closed.
The Russian Trading System of 24 leading shares rose by 0.22 percent to 184.35 on $26.49 million in volume.
"The market has been rising the whole day as brokers reacted to the good news -- now they are hoping that the International Monetary Fund will release the next tranche," one trader said.
Yeltsin surprised doctors with the speed of his recovery from a quintuple bypass on Tuesday. Leading U.S. surgeon Michael DeBakey said that in three or four months Yeltsin could be playing tennis.
Alexei Goncharov, chief analyst at Russian Brokerage House, said Western operators were a bit more cautious than their Russian counterparts, preferring to wait for more news on Yeltsin before buying.
"Leading Russian brokers bought the shares they hope will rise further after the holidays, after which the crucial time for Yeltsin will be over," he said.
"We are sure that if Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) gets up, walks and cracks a joke on Sunday, it will stimulate orders," he said.
An IMF mission arrives in Moscow this month to discuss paying Russia the next tranche of a $10 billion loan. It delayed payment of the tranche last month over concerns about poor tax revenues.
Khaleyev said Gazprom was the leading loser of the day, with prices falling to $0.410 from $0.434 at Tuesday's close following Tuesday's auction results.
A stake of 7.00 million shares in Gazprom was sold at an average 2,182.32 roubles ($0.400) a share, down from 2,870.06 roubles at the previous auction on October 30.
"I am surprised (the share price) has not fallen lower, but maybe it's because not everyone can participate in the auctions," Khaleyev said.
